You do not need the perfect prompt first time. Start from a clear request, look at the result and correct only what is missing. Here are three habits that change everything.

Propose 3 different titles and compare them for clarity and impact. Choosing between options is easier than correcting a single proposal.

lib.analisi-contratto.md:
---
name: analisi-contratto
description: Use this skill when you have to read a contract, an agreement or a set of terms and conditions in order to extract the duration, deadlines, renewals, withdrawal, penalties, obligations and points to watch, with a reference to the clauses.
---

# Analysis of a contract

## Warning
This analysis helps you read the contract but does not replace legal advice. Always say so at the end.

## Procedure
1. Identify the parties, the subject and the date.
2. Extract, with the reference clause and the exact sentence in quotation marks:
   - duration and expiry
   - automatic renewal and notice period for cancellation
   - withdrawal
   - penalties and limitations of liability
   - obligations on our side
   - payments and price adjustments
   - confidentiality and personal data
   - jurisdiction
3. Calculate the last date to cancel (expiry minus the notice period).
4. List the points to watch in plain words.

## Result
- A one-page sheet with the points above.
- A table of deadlines: event | date | clause.
- A “To clarify with the counterparty or a lawyer” list.

## Rules
- Use only the text of the contract. If a point is not there, write NOT PROVIDED FOR.
- Never interpret creatively: report and explain.
lib.analisi-contratto.quando: You extract deadlines, obligations and risks from contracts and terms and conditions.
lib.confronto-offerte.md:
---
name: confronto-offerte
description: Use this skill when you have to compare several quotes or supplier offers (PDF, Word, email) for the same purchase and prepare a comparison table with the differences and the questions to ask.
---

# Comparison of supplier quotes

## Before you start
- Ask what is being bought and which criteria matter most (price, timing, quality, warranty).
- If references/criteri-valutazione.md exists, use it.

## Procedure
1. From every quote extract: supplier, total price excluding VAT, items included, delivery times, warranty, payment terms, extra costs, validity.
2. For every piece of data give the page or the point of the quote it comes from.
3. Line up the items: flag what one quote includes and the others do not.
4. Calculate the comparable total cost (adding the declared extra costs).
5. List the important differences and the questions to ask each supplier.

## Result
- An Excel file: one row per quote, one column per criterion, a “page reference” column.
- A half-page summary: 3 key differences and the open questions.

## Rules
- Do not choose the supplier: prepare the comparison for whoever decides.
- Report prices and conditions exactly as written. Where a piece of data is missing write NOT STATED.

## Checks before delivering
- One row for every quote received.
- Every price has its page reference.
- The comparable totals are recalculated with code.
lib.confronto-offerte.quando: You compare quotes in different formats before choosing.
lib.estrazione-fatture.md:
---
name: estrazione-fatture
description: Use this skill when you have to extract into an Excel table the data of invoices, receipts, till receipts or delivery notes in PDF or image form, with a check on the totals.
---

# Extracting data from invoices and receipts

## Before you start
- Tell me how many documents you found and whether some are barely readable scans.
- Do not modify, move or delete the original documents.

## Procedure
1. From every document extract: file name, supplier, VAT number, number, date, net amount, VAT, total, payment due date.
2. Report the numbers and names exactly as they are written.
3. Check that net + VAT = total (tolerance €0.01); if scripts/controlla-totali.py exists, use it.
4. If a check does not add up, read the document again. After 2 attempts mark the row TO BE CHECKED.
5. Flag the possible duplicates (same supplier, number and amount).

## Result
An Excel file with:
- A “Dati” sheet: one row per document
- A “Da verificare” sheet: rows with problems and the reason
- A “Totali” sheet: totals by supplier and by month

## Rules
- Dates in DD/MM/YYYY format, amounts with 2 decimals.
- Never estimate an unreadable value: write TO BE CHECKED.

## Checks before delivering
- Number of rows = number of documents.
- No empty cells in the mandatory columns.
- All the totals verified or marked TO BE CHECKED.

name: presentazione-aziendale
description: Use this skill when you have to create a PowerPoint presentation from documents, notes or Excel data, using the company template (assets/modello.pptx) and the internal style rules.
---

# Presentation with the company template

## Before you start
- Ask: the audience, the duration, the goal of the presentation (to inform, to convince, to decide).
- You need the source material and the file assets/modello.pptx.

## Procedure
1. Read the material and identify the 3 main messages.
2. Propose the outline (the title and message of every slide) and WAIT for confirmation.
3. Create the slides with assets/modello.pptx: one idea per slide, a title that states the message.
4. Turn the important numbers into simple charts.
5. Write the speaker notes for every slide.

## Style rules
- 40 words per slide at most.
- 3 bullet points per slide at most.
- Charts with a title, the unit of measure and the source.
- Last slide: next steps or the decisions requested.

## Checks before delivering
- Every number matches the source material.
- No slide goes over 40 words.
- The colours, fonts and logo are the ones in the template.
- The number of slides suits the duration (about 1 slide every 2 minutes).

lib.pulizia-dati-excel.md:
---
name: pulizia-dati-excel
description: Use this skill when you have to clean an Excel or CSV list (customer records, contacts, items, price lists) of duplicates, empty cells, inconsistent formats and errors, before importing or using it.
---

# Cleaning up Excel lists

## Before you start
- Always work on a copy of the file.
- Tell me how many rows and columns you read and show me the first 5 rows.
- If references/regole-dati.md exists, use it for the formats and the mandatory fields.

## Procedure
1. Analyse and FLAG (without correcting): exact and likely duplicates, empty mandatory cells, invalid emails and phone numbers, dates and numbers in inconsistent formats, inconsistent spaces and capitals.
2. Show a summary of the problems with the number of rows involved and WAIT for confirmation.
3. Apply the confirmed corrections by running code.
4. Put the likely duplicates in a separate sheet, do not delete them.

## Result
An Excel file with:
- “Pulito”: the corrected list
- “Modifiche”: row | field | before | after
- “Da verificare”: doubtful rows and the reason

## Checks before delivering
- Clean rows + rows to check + duplicates removed = original rows.
- No empty mandatory cell in the “Pulito” sheet.
- Every change appears in the “Modifiche” sheet.

lib.report-mensile-excel.md:
---
name: report-mensile-excel
description: Use this skill when you have to prepare the monthly report for management starting from one or more Excel or CSV files (sales, costs, orders), with a comparison against the previous month and the decisions to be taken.
---

# Monthly report from Excel

## Before you start
- You need: this month's export, the previous month's export, any targets.
- If a file is missing, ask for it before going on.
- Tell me how many rows and columns you read in each file and the period covered.

## Procedure
1. Check the quality of the data: empty rows, duplicates, dates outside the period, negative amounts. List them, do not correct them silently.
2. Calculate by running code (if scripts/calcola-kpi.py exists, use it): total for the month, % change on the previous month, total by category.
   For the format of the report read references/esempio-report.md.
3. Compare every category with the target, if there is one.
4. Identify the 3 best and the 3 worst items, with the numerical reason.
5. Write a 3-line summary for people who have no time.
6. Propose at most 3 decisions, each one tied to a number.

## Result
A one-page Word document (use assets/modello-report.docx if present):
- Summary (3 lines)
- KPI table: item | month | previous month | % change | target
- A chart of the trend
- Proposed decisions
- Points to check

## Checks before delivering
- Every number matches the source files (re-check 3 numbers at random).
- The changes are calculated against the previous month.
- The report fits on one page.
- No invented data: where it is missing write NOT AVAILABLE.

lib.requisiti-app.md:
---
name: requisiti-app
description: Use this skill when someone wants to create an app, a management system, an online form or an automation and the idea has to be turned into a clear requirements document (PRD.md) before any code is written.
---

# Requirements for an app (PRD)

## Procedure
1. Interview the person with simple questions, ONE AT A TIME:
   - what problem it solves and what is done by hand today
   - who uses it (roles) and how many people
   - the 3–7 essential features
   - what data it handles and whether it is personal or confidential
   - access: open, by link, with a password, with different roles
   - from which devices (computer, phone)
   - connections with other tools (Excel, email, calendar)
   - what it must NOT do in the first version
2. Propose what to keep in the first version (MVP) and what to postpone.
3. Write PRD.md.

## Structure of PRD.md
- Goal and problem
- Users and roles
- Features of the first version (with verifiable acceptance criteria)
- Data handled and privacy
- Main screens (described in words)
- Out of scope for the first version
- Risks, costs to check, open questions
- Recommended type of app: a single HTML file, an app on the computer, an online app

## Rules
- Plain language, no unexplained technical terms.
- Verifiable acceptance criteria (e.g. “the user receives an email within 1 minute”).
- If there is personal data online, flag that IT and privacy must be involved.

lib.revisione-documento.md:
---
name: revisione-documento
description: Use this skill when you have to review a document before sending or publishing it (a letter, a quote, a report, a procedure, an article), checking mistakes, clarity, consistency and unverifiable statements.
---

# Reviewing and checking a document

## Procedure
1. Mistakes: spelling, punctuation, grammar.
2. Clarity: sentences over 25 words, jargon, ambiguous passages.
3. Consistency: numbers, dates and names the same throughout the document; totals that add up.
4. Statements to check: data, quotations, legal references, promises. For each one say whether it can be verified from the attached sources.
5. Tone: suitable for the stated recipient.

## Result
1. A table of changes: point | original text | proposal | reason.
2. A “To check before sending” list.
3. The corrected document (Word), without changing the content and style more than necessary.

## Rules
- Do not add new information.
- Do not change the meaning: if a point is unclear, propose something and ask.
- If references/guida-stile.md exists, follow it.

## Checks before delivering
- Every change is listed in the table.
- All the numbers in the document have been re-checked.
- The unverifiable statements are flagged.

name: risposte-richieste-frequenti
description: Use this skill when you have to reply to emails or messages with recurring questions (opening hours, delivery times, documents required, procedures, simple complaints) using the official information in references/informazioni.md.
---

# Replies to frequent requests

## Before you start
- Read references/informazioni.md: it is the only valid source for data, prices, timings and procedures.
- Read references/esempi-risposte.md to copy its tone and structure.

## Procedure
1. Work out what the message is really asking (there may be several questions).
2. Look for the answers in references/informazioni.md.
3. Write the reply: greeting, direct answer, any steps to take, closing.
4. If a question has no answer in references/informazioni.md, do NOT invent one: insert [TO BE CHECKED: …].
5. If the message is a serious complaint or contains legal threats, do not reply: flag that a person is needed.

## Style
- 150 words at most.
- Polite and direct tone, formal address (unless told otherwise).
- Short sentences, no bureaucratic formulas.

## Checks before delivering
- Every piece of data (price, date, time) is present in references/informazioni.md.
- Every question in the message has an answer or a [TO BE CHECKED].
- No promise that the procedures do not provide for.

lib.verbale-riunione.md:
---
name: verbale-riunione
description: Use this skill when you have to turn the transcript or the notes of a meeting (Teams, Meet, Zoom, handwritten notes) into minutes with decisions, actions, owners and deadlines.
---

# Meeting minutes

## Before you start
- You need: the transcript or the notes, the date, the topic. If possible, the list of participants.
- If the transcript is incomplete or confused in places, say so.

## Procedure
1. Identify the topics discussed, in the order in which they came up.
2. For every topic write a 2–3 line summary.
3. Extract the decisions taken (only the explicit ones).
4. Extract the actions: what, who, by when.
5. List the points left open and the questions without an answer.

## Result
A Word document, 2 pages at most:
- Header: date, participants, topic
- Summary
- Table of decisions
- Table of actions: action | owner | deadline | status
- Open points

## Rules
- Use only what was said. Do not attribute sentences or decisions to people who did not express them.
- Actions with no owner or date: write TO BE DEFINED.
- Neutral tone, no judgements about people.

## Checks before delivering
- Every decision and action can be found in the transcript.
- No action without an owner or a TO BE DEFINED.
- 2 pages at most.

ric.0.ott: The formula ready to paste, explained step by step, with the error case handled.
ric.0.p:
In Excel (Italian version) I have:
- sheet “Ordini”: item code in column B, quantity in column C
- sheet “Listino”: code in column A, price in column C

Write me the formula to put in Ordini!D2 to calculate quantity × the price from the price list.
Use the Italian function names (e.g. CERCA.X).
Explain it to me step by step and make sure that, if the code doesn't exist, it shows “CODICE MANCANTE” instead of an error.
ric.0.sit: You need to pull a price from one sheet into another, add up with conditions or work out deadlines, and you can't remember the formula.
ric.0.tip: Try the formula on 3 rows whose result you already know, before dragging it down the whole sheet.
ric.1.ott: The list of problems row by row and, once you confirm, the clean file with a record of the changes.
ric.1.p:
The attached file contains a list of [contacts / items / customers from our system].
First tell me how many rows and columns you have read.
Then find and FLAG, without correcting: duplicate rows (nearly identical ones too), empty cells in the required columns [list them], invalid emails or VAT numbers, dates and numbers in different formats.
Give me a table: row | problem | proposed correction.
After I confirm, give me back an Excel file with the sheets “Pulito”, “Modifiche” and “Da verificare”.
ric.1.sit: A contact list or item list with duplicates, empty cells and names written in different ways.
ric.1.t: Cleaning up a list full of duplicates and mistakes
ric.1.tip: Check that the rows in “Pulito” + “Da verificare” + the duplicates removed add up to the original total.
ric.10.ott: A place to ask “how do I…” and get answers quoted from the official documents.
ric.10.p:
[Upload every up-to-date manual and procedure to the project or notebook.]

Answer questions using ONLY the uploaded documents.
For every answer:
- state the document and page (or section)
- quote the exact sentence when it concerns rules or amounts
- if the documents contradict each other, show it and say which is the most recent
- if the answer is not there, write “not in the documents” and suggest who to ask.

First question: [e.g. what is the procedure for returning a faulty product?]
ric.10.sit: Procedures, manuals and rules scattered everywhere: colleagues keep asking the same questions.
ric.10.t: A knowledge base built on your internal manuals
ric.10.tip: When a procedure changes, replace the old document: otherwise the answers will mix up versions.
ric.11.ott: A Word procedure with numbered steps, responsibilities, typical mistakes and a flow diagram.
ric.11.p:
Turn these notes into a working procedure for a new colleague.
Structure: purpose; when it applies; who does what (simple RACI table); tools needed; numbered steps; mistakes to avoid; what to do if something goes wrong.
Add a flow diagram with the decision points (yes/no).
Where information is missing write [TO BE COMPLETED: question], do not invent it.
Give me back a Word document.

<notes>
[paste here]
</notes>
ric.11.sit: A procedure exists only in a colleague's head or in untidy notes.
ric.11.t: From scattered notes to a working procedure with a diagram
ric.11.tip: Have someone who has never done it follow the procedure to the letter: every doubt is a [TO BE COMPLETED].
ric.12.ott: A matrix linking every requirement to the answer, the document and the owner, with the uncovered requirements listed.
ric.12.p:
I am attaching the tender specification [and our own documents: company presentation, certifications, product sheets].
1. Extract ALL the requirements (mandatory and scored) with their reference: number each one.
2. Build an Excel matrix: no. | requirement | type (mandatory/scored) | points if stated | how we cover it | document that proves it | owner | status (covered / partial / uncovered).
3. Fill in “how we cover it” and “document” ONLY if the information is in our documents, otherwise “uncovered”.
4. List the uncovered requirements and the clarification questions to send before the stated deadline.
Check at the end that the number of requirements in the matrix matches those found in the specification.
ric.12.sit: A request for quotation with dozens of technical and administrative requirements: nothing must slip through.
ric.12.t: Response matrix for a tender or request for quotation
ric.12.tip: Re-read the specification at random: requirements hidden in annexes and footnotes are the easiest to miss.
ric.13.ott: A plain explanation, the deadlines, the documents required and a draft reply.
ric.13.p:

- what it asks of me and why
- by when (give the exact date)
- what happens if I do not reply
- which documents are needed
Then prepare a draft reply. If there are references to the law, quote them exactly as written and tell me to check them.

ric.13.tip: For fines, taxes or disputes use the explanation to understand, then talk to your adviser.

ric.17.p:

2. Give me back the improved version in PowerPoint, without changing the numbers.
3. Play the most critical member of the audience: 10 hard questions they could ask me, each with a short answer and the supporting data taken from the slides.
ric.17.sit: You already have the slides but they are full of text and you fear the hard questions.
ric.17.t: Improving a presentation and preparing for the questions
ric.17.tip: Rehearse out loud the 3 questions that put you in the most difficulty.
ric.18.ott: A web page in a single file, with clickable charts, filters and minimal text, to open or share.
ric.18.p:
Create an interactive web page in a single HTML file to present [the survey results / the sales trend].
Data: [paste the table or attach the CSV].
Content: title and main message; 3 large indicators; 2 interactive charts (they show the values on hover); a filter by [department/year]; a “What we do next” section.
Sober style, readable on a phone, no external service: it must work offline too.
Show me a preview and then give me the file to download.
ric.18.sit: You have to share results with people who will look at them on their own, on a computer or a phone.
ric.18.t: An interactive page instead of slides
ric.18.tip: Check that the numbers in the charts match the original table before sharing it.
ric.19.ott: A correct and polite reply, with no invented information.
ric.19.p:
Write a reply to this email: [paste the email].
Correct information to use: [paste].
Polite and direct tone, formal address, maximum 120 words.
If the email asks something that is not in the information, do not invent it: write [TO BE CHECKED].
ric.19.sit: Every day you get the same questions about lead times, documents, prices.
ric.19.t: A reply to a frequent request
ric.19.tip: If you use it often, turn it into a skill: look for “risposte-richieste-frequenti” in the library.
ric.2.ott: An Excel file with ready-made summaries, charts and a comment on the anomalies worth digging into.
ric.2.p:
I'm attaching vendite_2026.xlsx (one row per sale: date, product, category, shop, quantity, amount).
1. Tell me the rows you read, the period covered and any problems in the data.
2. Running code, create: sales by month; by category and month; by shop; the top 10 and bottom 10 products.
3. Spot the anomalies: months or shops with changes above 20%, products that collapse, sales with a zero or negative amount.
4. Give me back an Excel file with one sheet per summary, clear charts and a 10-line “Commento” sheet.
Keep the facts separate from your hypotheses about the causes.
ric.2.sit: You have a year's sales export and you need to understand what is going well, what isn't and why.
ric.2.t: Sales analysis with pivots, charts and anomalies
ric.2.tip: The causes the AI suggests are hypotheses: check them with the people who know the shops.
ric.20.ott: Two ready versions (one more formal, one more direct) to choose from.
ric.20.p:
Rewrite this email so that it is firm but polite: [paste the draft].
Goal: [get the payment by the 30th / turn down the request / clear up the mistake].
Context of the relationship: [e.g. long-standing supplier, first delay].
Propose 2 versions: one more formal and one more direct, maximum 150 words each. Explain the difference in one line.
ric.20.sit: You have to chase a payment, turn down a request or point out a mistake without damaging the relationship.
ric.20.t: A delicate email, in two versions
ric.20.tip: Read it imagining you are the recipient: if it would annoy you, ask for a third version.
ric.21.ott: 8 rules describing your style, ready to drop into your personal instructions, and a text written the way you would write it.
ric.21.p:
I am attaching 3 texts written by me: [emails / reports / quotes].
1. Analyse my style: sentence length, greetings, tone, recurring words, structure.
2. Describe it in 8 rules at most, ready to paste into my personal instructions.
3. Use those rules to write: [what you need].
ric.21.sit: The AI's answers “don't sound like you”.
ric.21.tip: Paste the rules into your personal instructions (lesson “Personalise your AI”).
ric.22.ott: A tidy newsletter, with headings, short texts and an appealing email subject line.
ric.22.p:
With the news below create the internal newsletter for [month].
Structure: email subject line (3 options); a 2-line opening; one section per item with a heading and 60 words maximum; “In brief” for the minor items; a closing with the next dates.
Friendly tone, informal address, no exaggerated hype. Do not add details that are not in the news.

<news>
[paste]
</news>
ric.22.sit: You have 6 pieces of news (a new colleague, results, procedures, events) in different emails and notes.
ric.22.t: An internal newsletter from scattered news
ric.22.tip: Check the names and job titles of the people mentioned: those are the mistakes people notice most.
ric.23.ott: An Excel file with a title, short description, long description and key points for every product.
ric.23.p:
The attached file contains the technical data of the products (one row per product).
For every product write: a title (max 60 characters), a short description (max 160 characters), a long description (80–120 words), 3 key points.
Rules: use ONLY the data in the row; no unproven claims (e.g. “the best”); tone [professional and concrete]; the same structure for all of them.
Start with 3 products and wait for my confirmation, then complete them all and give me back the Excel file with the new columns.
ric.23.sit: You have an Excel file with the technical data of 80 products and you need consistent descriptions.
ric.23.t: Product sheets for a catalogue or a website, in bulk
ric.23.tip: With many products, use the agent on your computer: the AI in chat can stop halfway through the list.
ric.24.ott: A calendar of 8 posts with the goal, a draft and a visual idea, in an Excel file.
ric.24.p:
We are [describe the company and the audience]. Goal for the month: [e.g. get known by new suppliers / attract candidates].
Create a plan of 8 LinkedIn posts (2 a week) in an Excel file: date | topic | goal | draft of the post (max 120 words) | image idea | closing call to action.
Vary the formats: a colleague's story, behind the scenes, an interesting figure, a practical tip.
No clichés and no excessive emoji. Use only the information I give you: [paste news and figures].
ric.24.sit: You want to post consistently but every week you start from scratch.
ric.24.t: A month of LinkedIn posts planned
ric.24.tip: Ask your colleagues for permission before quoting or photographing them.
ric.25.ott: An analysis of the points raised, a reply to the complaint and corrective actions with owners.
ric.25.p:
I am attaching the complaint we received and our account of the facts [paste].
1. List the points raised: for each one “justified / not justified / to be checked” with the reason, based only on the facts provided.
2. Write the reply: acknowledge what is justified, explain without over-defending, propose a concrete solution, maximum 250 words.
3. Propose internal corrective actions: action | owner | by when | how we check that it worked.
Flag whether the complaint contains legal or safety aspects that need an expert.
ric.25.sit: A detailed complaint, partly justified, that calls for a reply and internal action.
ric.25.tip: Do not send replies to complaints with legal implications without showing them to whoever handles those.
ric.26.ott: A report with the open schemes, the requirements, the deadlines and links to the official sources.
ric.26.p:
Search for the grants and public schemes open for [type of business, sector, region, size] for [investment: e.g. solar panels, digitalisation, training].
Use official sources (ministries, regional authorities, chambers of commerce, managing bodies) and give the link and the publication date.
For each scheme: body | grant | main requirements | eligible costs | deadline | link.
Flag the information that is old or uncertain and what to check with an adviser.
ric.26.sit: You have heard about grants for your business but you do not know which ones are open and whether they apply to you.
ric.26.t: Grants and public tenders with verifiable sources
ric.26.tip: Always open the official link: deadlines and requirements change often.
ric.27.ott: A comparison table with sources and dates, and the opportunities to stand out.
ric.27.p:
Analyse these competitors: [list with websites].
For each one, using only public information with a link and a date: services offered, prices stated (if public), who they target, declared strengths, recurring reviews (positive and negative).
Build a comparison table and, at the bottom, 5 opportunities for us to differentiate, given our offer: [describe your offer].
Write NOT FOUND where the information is not public.
ric.27.sit: You want to understand how 5 competitors position themselves on services, prices and communication.
ric.27.tip: Reviews are indicative: look at recurring trends, not single comments.
ric.28.ott: A table with weighted criteria and a list of what is still missing before deciding.
ric.28.p:
I have to choose between [option A, B, C] for [purpose].
Criteria that matter to me, with a weight from 1 to 5: [cost 5, time 3, …].
Build a comparison table with a weighted score, explaining each score with the information I gave you.
At the end state what is missing in order to decide and which questions to ask. Do not decide for me.
ric.28.sit: You have to choose between several solutions (software, suppliers, investments) and you want to think it through in an orderly way.
ric.28.tip: Change the weights and see whether the ranking changes: if it does, the choice depends on what really matters to you.
ric.29.ott: A risk register with probability, impact, prevention, plan B and owners.
ric.29.p:
We are starting this project: [description, timing, budget, people involved].
1. Identify 12–15 risks (technical, organisational, financial, supplier, people, regulatory).
2. For each one: probability (1–5) | impact (1–5) | priority | warning signs | preventive action | plan B | owner.
3. Build an Excel file sorted by priority and a probability × impact matrix.
4. Say which 3 risks to tackle this week.
Keep the risks that come from the data I gave you separate from the generic ones.
ric.29.sit: An important project is starting (a move, a new management system, opening a site).
ric.29.tip: Review the register every month: a risk that is not updated is a risk that is forgotten.
ric.3.ott: The list of matched transactions, the unmatched ones and the likely mistakes.
ric.3.p:
I'm attaching two files: estratto_conto.xlsx (date, description, amount) and registro_pagamenti.xlsx (date, supplier, invoice number, amount).
Running code, match the transactions using the amount and the date (3-day tolerance) and, where useful, the name in the description.
Create an Excel file with the sheets:
- “Abbinati”: bank transaction | record | criterion used
- “Solo in banca”
- “Solo nel registro”
- “Dubbi”: possible but uncertain matches, with the reason
At the end summarise the totals of each sheet and check that they match the totals of the two files.
ric.3.sit: The bank total doesn't match the payments register and you have to find the differences.
ric.3.t: Reconciling a bank statement with recorded payments
ric.3.tip: The “Dubbi” matches have to be checked by hand, one by one.
ric.30.ott: A dossier with verified public information, risk signals and questions to ask.
ric.30.p:
Gather public information about the company [name, city, VAT number if known]:
- company details and years in business
- relevant news from the last 3 years
- declared certifications
- reviews and reputation
- any risk signals (litigation, frequent name changes, very negative reviews)
Every piece of information with a source and a date. Distinguish what is verified from what is only claimed by the company.
Close with 8 questions to ask the supplier and the documents to request (e.g. company registry extract, compliance certificates, references).
ric.30.sit: You are about to entrust an important job to a company you do not know.
ric.30.t: Checking a new supplier before signing
ric.30.tip: Registry extracts and official documents have to be requested and checked: the online search is only the first filter.
ric.31.ott: The same answer with the statements classified and the unverifiable ones flagged.
ric.31.p:
Reread your previous answer like a strict reviewer.
For every statement, say whether it is:
- taken from the documents I gave you (with page or section)
- taken from the web (with a link)
- your own inference or general knowledge
Flag numbers, dates, names, citations and legal references that you can’t verify.
Then rewrite the answer: remove or mark as TO CHECK everything that isn’t verifiable.
ric.31.sit: You have an answer from the AI that you have to base a decision on.
ric.31.tip: Better still in a new chat, where the AI is not “attached” to the answer.
ric.32.ott: A small app in the browser: you enter the values and get the price with the breakdown and the text for the email.
ric.32.p:
Create a small app in a single HTML file: “Quote calculator”.
Fields: job description; material rows (description, quantity, unit cost, with an “add row” button); working hours and hourly rate; transport km and cost per km; margin %; VAT %.
Result: a breakdown table, net total, VAT, grand total; a “Copy text for the email” button with a polite summary.
Italian number format (1.234,56 €). No external service, it must work offline. Show me the preview.
ric.32.sit: You work out every quote by hand with materials, hours, transport and margin, and sometimes you get it wrong.
ric.32.tip: Check the calculation against an old quote whose total you already know.
ric.33.ott: A checklist you can tick off from your phone too, with notes, date and a printable summary.
ric.33.p:
Create an app in a single HTML file: “Checklist [closing the shop]”.
Items divided into sections: [paste the list of checks].
Features: a tick box for every item, a notes field, the name of whoever fills it in, automatic date and time, a progress bar, a “Print / save the summary as PDF” button, a “Start again” button.
Large and readable on a phone. The data stays only on the device. No external service.
ric.33.sit: Opening and closing the shop, safety checks, setting up an event: always the same steps, sometimes forgotten.
ric.33.t: An interactive checklist to use every day
ric.33.tip: Save it on your phone as a shortcut on the Home screen so you can open it instantly.
ric.34.ott: An interactive quiz with questions taken from the manual, an explanation of every answer and a final score.
ric.34.p:
From the attached manual create a training quiz in a single HTML file.
- 15 multiple-choice questions on the most important points (safety and common mistakes first)
- after every answer: right/wrong, an explanation and the page of the manual
- a final score, a list of the topics to revise, a “try again” button that shuffles the questions and the answers
Use only the content of the manual. No external service. Show me the list of questions first so I can approve them.
ric.34.sit: New colleagues have to learn procedures and safety rules, and you want to check they have understood them.
ric.34.t: A training quiz from a manual
ric.34.tip: Have the questions checked by someone who knows the procedures: a wrong quiz teaches mistakes.
ric.35.ott: A page you open, load the CSV into and immediately see indicators, charts and filters, without sending any data online.
ric.35.p:
Create an app in a single HTML file: “Monthly dashboard”.
The user loads a CSV file with these columns: [date; department; product; quantity; amount] (semicolon separator, decimals with a comma).
Show: 4 indicators (total, change on the previous month, best product, best department); a chart of the trend by day; a chart by department; a filterable and sortable table; a button to export the filtered table as CSV.
Everything must work in the browser without sending the data and without libraries from the internet. Handle errors clearly if the file has the wrong columns.
ric.35.sit: Every month you export a CSV from your management software and redo the same charts by hand.
ric.35.t: A mini dashboard from a CSV file
ric.35.tip: Try it with a CSV whose totals you already know, then with a “dirty” one to see whether the errors are clear.
ric.36.ott: An app on your computer that reads the invoices, renames them “date_supplier_number” and moves them into monthly folders, with an Excel log.
ric.36.p:
Build a local app for my computer: “Invoice archive”.
Input: a folder chosen by the user containing invoice PDFs (scans too).
For every PDF: read the supplier, the number and the date (use OCR if the text is not selectable, with open-source programs).
Rename to YYYY-MM-DD_Supplier_Number.pdf and move into subfolders by year and month.
Create registro.xlsx: old name | new name | supplier | number | date | status (ok / to be checked).
Rules: make a backup copy of the folder first; files not read with certainty go into “da-verificare” without being renamed; no data sent over the internet.
A simple interface in the browser with a “Start” button and a final summary. Before writing any code, ask me the questions you need.
ric.36.sit: You download dozens of invoices with incomprehensible names and file them by hand.
ric.36.t: An app that renames and files invoice PDFs
ric.36.tip: Try it on a copy of 10 invoices, check the log, and only then use it on the real folder.
ric.37.ott: An app that merges everything into one file, standardises the columns and produces an error report to send back to the sites.
ric.37.p:
Build a local app: “Merge branches”.
Input: a folder with one Excel file per branch (file name = branch name). Expected columns: date, product code, description, quantity, amount.
Features:
- recognises columns with similar names (e.g. “Qty” = quantity) and asks for confirmation the first time
- merges everything, adding a Branch column
- checks for: dates outside the month, negative quantities, codes that do not exist in listino.xlsx, duplicate rows
- creates riepilogo.xlsx (data, totals by branch and product) and errori.xlsx (branch, row, problem)
Do not modify the original files. Interface in the browser with step-by-step instructions. Save the versions with Git.
ric.37.sit: Every month you receive Excel files from the sites, with small differences in the columns, and you merge them by hand.
ric.37.t: An app that merges the branches' Excel files and flags the errors
ric.37.tip: The errori.xlsx sheet is the real added value: send it to the branches so they fix things at the source.
ric.38.ott: An app that, once you choose the template and the list, creates all the Word/PDF documents while checking for missing fields.
ric.38.p:
Build a local app: “Document generator”.
- The user chooses a Word template with fields in curly brackets (e.g. {NAME}, {AMOUNT}, {START_DATE}) and an Excel file with one row per document.
- The app shows which template fields have no matching column and blocks until everything is linked.
- A preview of the first 3 documents, then generation of all of them in Word and PDF, with a configurable file name (e.g. {SURNAME}_{NAME}).
- Italian formats for dates and amounts.
- Final report: documents created, rows with empty fields (not generated).
No data on the internet. A simple interface in the browser, a start file to double-click and a README.md.
ric.38.sit: You prepare contracts, engagement letters or certificates that are all the same except for a few details.
ric.38.t: A document generator from a Word template and an Excel list
ric.38.tip: Open and compare 3 generated documents with the Excel data before sending them.
ric.39.ott: An online app with logins for staff and managers, approvals, a calendar and a monthly export.
ric.39.p:
I am attaching the requirements document PRD.md [created in the lesson “Building complete apps”].
Build the “Holiday requests” app following the PRD:
- first propose a plan in stages and the technologies, with the expected monthly costs, and wait for my confirmation
- stage 1: screens with dummy data; stage 2: database and login with roles; stage 3: notification emails; stage 4: Excel export
- after every stage stop and tell me how to test it
- security: no passwords in the code, every employee sees only their own requests, the manager only their own department
- at the end walk me step by step through publishing it and write a README.md for maintenance.
ric.39.sit: Holidays are requested by email and tracked in a hand-updated Excel file: requests get lost and overlap.
ric.39.t: An online app for holiday and leave requests
ric.39.tip: Before going live with real data, involve IT and privacy: these are employees' personal data.
ric.4.ott: An Excel file with a cautious, expected and optimistic scenario, every assumption editable, and a summary for management.
ric.4.p:
I'm attaching the data of the last 3 years (revenue and costs by month and by item).
Build a 2027 budget model in Excel:
- sheet “Ipotesi”: revenue growth, cost inflation, hires, investments. All in editable, highlighted cells.
- sheets “Prudente”, “Atteso”, “Ottimista” calculated with FORMULAS that read the assumptions (not values typed in by hand).
- sheet “Sintesi”: margin, cash month by month, a chart of the three scenarios.
Suggest starting values for the assumptions, justifying them with the historical data, and point out which assumptions weigh most on the result.
ric.4.sit: You have to prepare next year's budget and show what happens if things go better or worse.
ric.4.t: A budget with three scenarios and explicit assumptions
ric.4.tip: Change one assumption and check that all the scenarios update: that means the formulas are properly linked.
ric.40.ott: An online app where a ticket is opened with a photo, assigned to a technician and tracked through to closure.
ric.40.p:
I want an online app “Reports” for [maintenance / internal IT].
First write the PRD.md asking me questions one at a time, then build it in stages.
Planned features:
- open a ticket from a phone: category, location, description, photo, urgency
- assignment to a technician, statuses (new, in progress, waiting, closed), comments
- an automatic email to whoever opened the ticket at every status change
- a filterable list and monthly statistics (average closure times by category)
- roles: reporter, technician, manager
State the monthly cost of the services and how to make backups. Stop after every stage so I can try it.
ric.40.sit: Faults and requests arrive by word of mouth or on WhatsApp and get lost.
ric.40.t: Internal support tickets with photos from a phone
ric.40.tip: Start with a single site or a single department for a month, then widen it.
ric.41.ott: An Excel file with one row per expense, totals by category and doubtful or duplicate documents flagged.
ric.41.p:
The “originali” folder contains photos and PDFs of this month's receipts.
Create risultati/nota_spese.xlsx: File | Date | Merchant | Category (Fuel, Meals, Transport, Accommodation, Other) | Amount | Payment.
Rules: amounts and dates exactly as written, never estimated; unreadable documents → TO BE CHECKED; do not touch the originals.
Checks: number of rows = number of files; amounts with 2 decimals or TO BE CHECKED; totals by category and overall at the bottom.
Final report: TO BE CHECKED documents and possible duplicates (same date, merchant and amount).
ric.41.sit: Photos and PDFs of the month's receipts to turn into an expense report by category.
ric.41.tip: Check 3 amounts at random and every possible duplicate.
ric.42.ott: Files organised by type and year, clear names, a log of the changes and not a single file lost.
ric.42.p:
The folder “da-ordinare” (a COPY) contains about 300 mixed files.
1. Analyse it and propose the structure of subfolders and 10 examples of new names (YYYY-MM-DD_description). Wait for my confirmation.
2. Carry it out and create risultati/registro.xlsx: old name | new name | folder.
Rules: do not delete anything; possible duplicates into “possibili-doppioni”; unrecognised files into “da-controllare”.
Checks: the number of files before and after must be identical; every file must appear in the log.
ric.42.sit: A shared folder (or your Downloads) full of mixed-up documents with incomprehensible names.
ric.42.t: Tidying up a folder of 300 files
ric.42.tip: Work on a copy: only replace the original folder when the result convinces you.
ric.43.ott: An Excel file with expiry dates, renewals, notice periods and last dates to cancel, sorted by urgency.
ric.43.p:
The “contratti” folder contains contracts in PDF and Word.
Create risultati/scadenzario.xlsx: File | Counterparty | Subject | Expiry | Automatic renewal | Notice period | Last date to cancel | Annual amount | Penalties | Reference clause.
Rules: only what is written; NOT STATED where it is missing; a clause or page for every piece of data.
Checks: one row per file; last date = expiry − notice period; no empty cells.
Stop: a contract that is unreadable after 2 attempts → TO BE CHECKED.
In the chat: the contracts to cancel or renew in the next 90 days.
ric.43.sit: Dozens of contracts (suppliers, insurance, leases) and nobody knows when they expire or renew themselves.
ric.43.t: A deadline register from a folder of contracts
ric.43.tip: Open the 5 most expensive contracts and check the expiry and the notice period: those are the ones that matter.
ric.44.ott: The list of required documents with those found, missing or expired, and an index of the file.
ric.44.p:
The “requisiti” folder contains the list of documents required by the audit [e.g. an ISO 9001 or safety checklist].
The “documenti” folder contains COPIES of our documents.
1. For every requirement find the document that satisfies it (by reading its content, not just its name).
2. Create risultati/verifica_audit.xlsx: requirement | document found | page | date of the document | status (present / expired / partial / missing) | note.
3. Treat as expired the documents whose revision is older than [12] months or whose validity dates have passed.
4. Create risultati/indice_fascicolo.docx with an ordered list of the documents present.
Do not modify the documents. In the chat: the missing and expired requirements, in order of importance.
ric.44.sit: The inspection or audit is coming (quality, safety, privacy) and you have to prove you have every document.
ric.44.t: A file ready for an audit or a certification
ric.44.tip: “Partial” and “missing” are the to-do list before the audit: assign them straight away.
ric.45.ott: A filled-in Excel file with the data, the links and the date of collection, and the incomplete rows flagged.
ric.45.p:
For each of these suppliers [list of websites] collect from their public sites:
product [precise description] | price excluding VAT | unit | minimum quantity | delivery times | shipping costs | link to the page | date of collection.
Rules: only information visible on the site, no password logins, no forms to submit.
Checks: every price has its link; where the information is not public write NOT PUBLISHED.
Stop: if a site asks you to register or does not load after 2 attempts, flag it and move on to the next.
Deliver the Excel file and a summary of the 3 best offers on equal conditions.
ric.45.sit: You have to compare prices, lead times and conditions published on 15 supplier websites.
ric.45.t: Collecting data from several websites into one Excel file
ric.45.tip: Online prices change: keep the date of collection and reconfirm before ordering.
ric.46.ott: A repeatable task (and, if the tool allows it, a scheduled one) that prepares the report ready for you to check.
ric.46.p:
Every Monday the “settimana” folder contains the updated exports: ordini.xlsx and consegne.xlsx.
Prepare risultati/report_settimana_[date].docx with:
- orders received and delivered this week, compared with the previous week
- late orders (expected delivery date passed) with the customer and the days of delay
- 3 points to watch
Checks: the totals must match the files; no order counted twice; if a file is missing or old (modified more than 3 days ago) stop and warn me.
Do not send any email: just prepare the document and a draft message in the chat.
At the end suggest how to turn this work into a skill and, if your tool allows it, into a task scheduled every Monday at 8.
ric.46.sit: Every Monday you take the same files, do the same sums and send the same kind of summary.
ric.46.t: A weekly report that prepares itself
ric.46.tip: For the first 4 weeks check the report before using it; after that a spot check is enough.
ric.47.ott: A summary, the decisions, the actions with owners and the open points.
ric.47.p:
From the attached transcript create:
- a 5-line summary
- the decisions taken
- the actions: what | who | by when
- the open points
Use only what was actually said. Where the owner or the date is missing write TO BE DEFINED.
ric.47.sit: You have the automatic transcript of an hour-long meeting.
ric.47.tip: Always tell the participants before recording or transcribing a meeting.
ric.48.ott: The goal, an agenda with timings, the questions and the material to send in advance.
ric.48.p:
I have to hold a meeting about [topic] with [participants and roles], lasting [minutes].
Goal: [to decide / to align / to gather ideas].
Prepare for me: the goal in one sentence; an agenda with timings; for every item the question it has to answer; the material to send in advance; the text of the invitation.
ric.48.sit: An important meeting and the risk of an hour of discussion with no decisions.
ric.48.tip: Put the decisions to be taken in the first 20 minutes, while attention is high.
ric.49.ott: An Excel file with tasks, dependencies, owners, dates and a Gantt chart.
ric.49.p:
Project: [description], end date: [date], people: [roles].
1. Break it down into phases and tasks (30 at most), each with an estimated duration, an owner and the task it depends on.
2. Calculate the dates backwards from the deadline and flag the critical tasks (those with no slack).
3. Give me back an Excel file with the table and a Gantt chart with bars coloured by phase.
4. State the 3 intermediate milestones to keep an eye on.
The durations are estimates: put them in an editable column that updates the dates.
ric.49.sit: A project with several people and deadlines (a move, a product launch, an event).
ric.49.t: A project plan with tasks and a Gantt chart
ric.49.tip: Have the durations reviewed by the people who will actually do the work: they are usually optimistic.
ric.5.ott: Instructions (or the file itself) with drop-down menus, validity checks, warning colours and an instructions sheet.
ric.5.p:
I have a shared Excel sheet for recording material requests: date, department, item, quantity, urgency, notes.
Turn it into a mistake-proof form:
- drop-down menus for department, item (from an “Elenchi” sheet) and urgency
- validation: the date can't be in the past, quantity a whole number between 1 and 500
- conditional formatting: urgent rows in red, empty required fields in yellow
- protection for the formulas and an “Istruzioni” sheet
Explain the steps to do it in Excel in Italian, or give me back the file ready made.
ric.5.sit: Several colleagues fill in the same Excel file and each writes the data their own way.
ric.5.t: Turning a spreadsheet into a mistake-proof form
ric.5.tip: Have a colleague fill in the form with no explanation: wherever they go wrong, a check is missing.
ric.50.ott: A day-by-day plan, a checklist for the manager and the documents to prepare.
ric.50.p:
A new [role] is joining the [department] department. I am attaching the job description and the main procedures.
Create:
1. a plan for the first 30 days: week | goals | activities | with whom | how we check
2. a checklist for the manager (before arrival, first day, end of the first week, end of the month)
3. a list of the access rights and equipment to prepare
4. 5 questions to ask the new colleague at the end of the month
A Word document, with a welcoming and concrete tone.
ric.50.sit: A new person arrives and every time the onboarding is improvised.
ric.50.t: Onboarding a new colleague in the first 30 days
ric.50.tip: Turn it into a skill: the next onboarding will take 5 minutes.
ric.51.ott: A job advert, interview questions tied to the skills and a scoring grid.
ric.51.p:
I have to hire a [role]. Essential skills: [list]. Useful skills: [list].
Create:
1. a clear advert (max 250 words, hours, location, what we offer)
2. 10 interview questions based on concrete examples (“tell me about a time when…”), linked to the skills
3. a scoring grid: skill | what to listen for to give a score of 1, 3, 5
Inclusive language, no unnecessary requirements (age, gender, origin).
Do not assess the candidates yourself and do not ask me for candidates' personal data.
ric.51.sit: You have to hire and you want to assess the candidates consistently and fairly.
ric.51.t: Recruiting: the advert, the interview questions and a scoring grid
ric.51.tip: Do not upload CVs containing personal data into tools your company has not approved.
ric.6.ott: Percentages per question, the recurring themes in the comments with examples, and 3 conclusions.
ric.6.p:
The attached file contains the answers to a survey (multiple-choice questions and free-text answers).
1. Using code, calculate the percentages for each multiple-choice question, also by [department / site].
2. Group the free-text answers into 5–7 themes: for each one the number of mentions and 2 real examples.
3. Write 3 conclusions and 3 possible actions, keeping the data separate from the interpretations.
Give me back an Excel file with the results and a one-page summary in Word.
Don't quote sentences that would make it possible to recognise who wrote them.
ric.6.sit: You have 300 answers to a satisfaction or staff survey, with a lot of written comments.
ric.6.t: Analysing a survey with free-text answers
ric.6.tip: Read 20 original comments at random to check that the themes are right.
ric.7.ott: One page with a summary, the points to watch and the decisions required, with page references.
ric.7.p:
Summarise the attached document for management:
- a 5-line summary
- 3 points to watch
- decisions required, with the deadline if stated
One page maximum. Say which page each piece of information comes from.
If something isn't clear in the document, flag it instead of interpreting it.
ric.7.sit: A 30-page document that management needs to know about without reading it all.
ric.7.t: A summary for people with no time
ric.7.tip: Open 2 of the pages cited and check that they really say what the summary says.
ric.8.ott: A table with every difference and what it means in practice.
ric.8.p:
I'm attaching two versions of the same document: [v1] and [v2].
List EVERY difference in a table: section | text before | text after | practical impact for us.
Don't skip small changes to numbers, dates, amounts, obligations and words like “may/must”.
At the end, point out the 3 most important changes.
ric.8.sit: You've received the new version of a contract, a policy or an offer and you want to know what has changed.
ric.8.t: Comparing two versions of the same document
ric.8.tip: For important contracts, have the relevant changes checked by whoever handles the legal side.
ric.9.ott: A checklist of the requirements, the list of documents to prepare and a calendar of deadlines, with references.
ric.9.p:
I'm attaching the text of [the call for funding / the regulation].
Use only the document. For each point give the article or page and the exact sentence in quotation marks.
Create:
1. A checklist of the requirements to take part (or to be compliant): requirement | reference | does it apply to us? (leave blank)
2. Documents to prepare: document | who provides it | reference
3. Deadlines: date | what to do | reference
4. Ambiguous points to clarify with the authority
Give me everything in an Excel file and write NON INDICATO where the document says nothing.
ric.9.sit: A 60-page call for funding or a new regulation: you need to work out the requirements, the documents and the deadlines.
ric.9.t: From a call for funding or a regulation to a checklist and deadlines
ric.9.tip: Dates are the most delicate part: check every one of them against the original text.
